# Duration weights (seconds) for the self-host e2e shard partition —
# consumed by scripts/selfhost-shard-tests (greedy LPT). Only tests that
# are meaningfully slower than the ~0.1-1s norm need an entry; everything
# else defaults to weight 1.
#
# Baseline heavy entries measured on the x86_64 ubuntu-latest lane with
# all drivers warm (2026-07-11, run 29157258229); the IR / wasm mid-tier
# and the wasmtime-gated entries added from run 29165757576 (the first
# with wasmtime restored to the shards).
#
# STALENESS IS NOT BENIGN. A wrong/missing/extra entry cannot drop or
# double-run a test — the partition always covers the real -test.list
# output — but a BADLY wrong one pushes its shard past the job timeout,
# which fails the shard for real, deterministically, on unrelated
# commits. That has happened twice: TestSelfHostInterpDriverX86_64 at 7
# against ~166 s (#5914) and TestSelfHostAssumeEligibleByteIdenticalX86_64
# with no entry at all against 482-738 s (#6823).
#
# NOTHING USED TO MEASURE THIS, which is why "update opportunistically"
# meant "update after a shard dies". The `verify` job now audits this file
# against the durations the shards report (scripts/ci-test-weights) and
# prints a corrected-weights block in its job summary. Paste from that
# block rather than guessing — it only ever raises a weight, for the
# reason in the next paragraph.
#
# WEIGHT PESSIMISTICALLY. The same test measured 482 s and 738 s on
# consecutive runs; its entry is the slower of the two. What matters to
# LPT is RELATIVE order, so uniform drift is harmless and NON-UNIFORM
# drift is what bites — which is why a single generous entry is safe and
# a single mean one is not.
#
# Three entries (InterpDriver, LoadFixpoint, ModloadPerModuleWholeCompiler)
# were re-measured locally on 2026-07-30; everything else still carries its
# 2026-07-11 figure, so treat the rest as unverified rather than current
# until an audit run reports on it.
#
# DO NOT TRUST A LOCALLY-COMPUTED SHARD INDEX. Reconstructing the
# partition locally from `go test -list` disagrees with CI about which
# bucket a test lands in, because that union does not exactly match the
# one CI derives from its prebuilt binaries. The shard NUMBER is not
# reproducible outside CI; the mis-weighting is, and giving a heavy test
# its own bucket is the remedy whichever bucket that turns out to be.
#
# NOTE on the TestSelfHostExtern* family: those ~39 tests each build a
# stdin driver that is byte-identical to the stock wasm_runio_run.fern,
# which the `wasm*` warm jobs prime — so post-conversion each restores
# the driver (~1s) and its remaining cost is just its own wasmtime +
# wasm-tools compose run (~5-10s). They no longer need per-test weights;
# left at the default 1 unless a shard log shows them dominating again.

# A weight cannot buy a test more wall than the shard job has (#6667). When the
# honest cost is a large fraction of the shards' `-test.timeout`, the remedy is
# OWN_JOB_TESTS in test-e2e-selfhost.yml, not a bigger number here — those names
# are filtered out before the partition sees them, so an entry for one is dead.
# TestSelfHostWasmWholeCompilerShardedLink went that way: weighted 240 from a
# 170 s local measurement, it still ran 12.8 min in CI and timed out its shard.
# TestSelfHostModloadPerModuleWholeCompilerArm64 followed at ~945 s measured in
# CI against an entry of 80 — 87% of the shards' wall for one test.

# Whole-compiler self-builds / fixpoints — the genuine multi-minute tail.
TestSelfHostModloadPerModuleWholeCompilerX86_64 460
# 18 whole-compiler modules emitted twice (with and without -assume-eligible)
# and compared byte-for-byte. It carried NO entry — so LPT ranked ~10 minutes of
# work as 1 s — and the shard holding it ran 13 min on run 31758666459 (482 s)
# and blew the 18-minute timeout on run 31759653118 (738 s), where the partition
# happened to pair it with a heavier complement. Weighted at the slower of the
# two: it varies by ~50% run to run, so give it the pessimistic bucket.
TestSelfHostAssumeEligibleByteIdenticalX86_64 738
# Two whole-compiler emit-all passes at batch=4. MEASURED 424 s by the audit on
# run 31782687541, against an entry of 130 — the same shape as the two incidents
# above, caught this time before it failed anything. Still under the entry above,
# so it does not set the max-shard wall.
TestSelfHostPerModuleEmitAllFixpointBatch4X86_64 638
# Two warm drivers (asm_ir_run + wasm_ir_run), 14 subtests that are ~0.01s each —
# the cost is almost entirely the driver restore.
TestSelfHostFnArrayFieldGateX86_64 12
TestSelfHostFnArrayFieldGateWasm 12
TestSelfHostTupleFnZeroArgIRX86_64 12
TestSelfHostTupleFnZeroArgIRWasm 12
TestSelfHostFnValueCaptureIRX86_64 25
TestSelfHostFnValueCaptureWasmIR 25
TestSelfHostAsmIRPath 28
TestSelfHostStdTestE2E 18
# Not a driver-restore cost like the block above: MEASURED 128 s against an entry
# of 55 (audit, run 31782687541).
TestSelfHostFieldReclaimIRX86_64 193

# Tests the first audit run (31782687541) found above the 60 s threshold with no
# entry at all, weighted at its measurement plus the standard band. Each was
# being partitioned as 1 s.
TestSelfHostIRVerifyGateWholeCompiler 179
TestSelfHostStage2Compiler 175
TestSelfHostIRVerifyProvidedCorpusClean 144
TestSelfHostArm64NativeMmcMatchesCrossHost 124

# Tuple element from a wide-returning call (#5902): 7 subtests through two
# drivers (asm_run + asm_pathprobe_run). MEASURED 2.6 s with both restored from
# the warm cache, per the FERN_SELFHOST_BUILD_CACHE method documented on the
# interp-driver entry below — a cold `go test` reports 249 s, 94x higher,
# because it re-emits both drivers.
TestSelfHostTupleWideCallElem 3
# The interp driver (#5912): self-host-compiles lexer + parser + interp + util
# into a working interpreter, then feeds it 104 tiny programs. MEASURED 6.58 s
# with the modload driver restored from the warm cache, which is what the shard
# step configures via FERN_SELFHOST_BUILD_CACHE.
#
# Recorded because the naive measurement is off by ~23x and I nearly wrote it
# here: `go test` with no FERN_SELFHOST_BUILD_CACHE has NO disk cache at all
# (diskCacheReadDirs returns nil), so it re-emits the whole driver every
# invocation and reports ~140-155 s. Almost all of that is the driver build the
# warm artifact eliminates. To reproduce the real number, point the var at a dir
# already holding `<hash>.driverbin` — note the suffix, `drv-<hash>` is the
# separate link cache and will silently MISS.
#
# This test had no entry while it was segfaulting on every integer literal
# (#5901, fixed by #5908), so its 18-minute shard-11 blowout was the hang, not a
# scheduling error. 6.58 s is the honest cost; the entry is ordinary balance.
TestSelfHostInterpDriverX86_64 170
# The arm64 native-assembler lane (the branch-veneer coverage): builds
# asm_modload_run for arm64 through the in-process pure-Go assembler — a
# ~135 MB image — then runs it. No warm artifact applies (the warm jobs
# build x86 host drivers), so this is a genuine cold build every shard.
# MEASURED 117 s locally, of which ~110 s is the emit+assemble.
TestSelfHostArm64ModloadNativeBuild 120
# Executes the self-host arm64 __fern_proc_exec blob from both emitters.
# Dominated by the one modload driver build it shares with the rest of the
# suite; MEASURED 108 s cold, near-free once that driver is warm.
TestSelfHostArm64ProcExecRuns 15
# `TestSelfHostStage2FixedPointArm64` sat here at 900 — a real measurement
# (run 30581856560: 53 s of stage-1/stage-2 build, then `self` 709 s of mmc2
# re-emitting the compiler under qemu) for a test that had already been
# deleted with `asm_arm64_load_run.fern` in #5972. Four other entries were
# dead the same way. They cost nothing — the sharder only weights names its
# `-test.list` input actually contains — but they read as coverage, and the
# same staleness in `test-e2e-arm64.yml` was load-bearing there (#6310).
# `make testnames` now fails on a name in .github/ that matches no test, so
# an entry cannot outlive its test again.

# Builds no driver: it interprets the self-host front end once per case
# through the native `-interp`, so its cost is the 14 cases, not a compile.
# Measured 26 s locally (4-core, machine busy); weighted pessimistically.
TestSelfHostFrontEndNumericLiteralCodes 60

# The corpus formatter-parity leg: one `-fmt` of each of the 425 .fern files
# under examples/ + internal/stdlib through the linked driver. MEASURED 16 s
# locally for the whole sweep (the driver's fixed startup is ~12 ms; the cost is
# the ten 15-50 kloc self_host modules), on top of the fern.fern driver the two
# older fmt tests already warm. Weighted generously against a cold cache.
TestSelfHostFmtCorpusParityX86_64 60

# The two host-independent fmt legs: they drive fern.fern through the native
# `-interp` rather than linking a driver, so no gcc and no x86-64 host. MEASURED
# 28 s and 2.5 s locally over the 32 parity cases and the two -w / -d cases.
TestSelfHostFmtWrittenFormViaInterp 60
TestSelfHostFmtWriteAndDiffViaInterp 15
